# AL-68 iteration02 independent behavior discovery

Outcome: CHANGES_REQUESTED for scoped code correctness. Overall runtime acceptance remains INCOMPLETE separately; parent owns integrated make and delivery.

Run: iter02-behavior-sol-01. Phase: discovery, independent first pass. Candidate: frozen candidate-02-01, base de31cb1 (de31cb158cb9566131eda45a8a4d5008972d5b98); supplied diff /tmp/al68-iter02-candidate-01.diff and exact snapshot /tmp/al68-iter02-candidate-01-xf13oa7x/paths.json. Requested settings: codex / gpt-6.1-sol / high. Dispatch request is distinct from runtime observation; no independent provider telemetry, usage or cost measurement was performed.

Read behavior persona, shared review context, review procedure, technical guidelines, regression boundaries, frozen CONTRACT and approved iteration02 PLAN. Did not read sibling reports, iteration02 REVIEW/REVIEW_RUNS or iteration03 PLAN. Formed source hypotheses before consulting /tmp/al68-iter02-corrections-02.md. Initial Git status contained staged candidate paths, staged iteration03 plan, parent ticket edits and untracked review archives; preserved all. Only assigned report and disposable /tmp probes were written. No children, staging, commits, telemetry, trust changes or installation into real harness projects.

## Findings

### B1 — P1: Baseline validation does not enforce ticket ownership

Locations: backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture_worker.go:221-242 (validateGenerationProject), called from backend/cmd/agentic-lens/main.go:237-248; merge at main.go:383-439.

Trigger: Two explicitly bound roots in one physical project, rootA bound TEST-100 and rootB bound TEST-200. Copy the valid TEST-100 ledger into TEST-200's canonical output (or accidentally select the first ledger as the second ticket's output), then publish TEST-200 automatically/manually.

Expected: Exact ticket ownership applies to baseline owners as well as fresh selectors. A copied other-ticket baseline must be rejected or explicitly recovered; project membership alone cannot associate its owners with the requested ticket.

Observed: Native generate --capture-auto --ticket-id TEST-200 exits successfully, rewrites ticket_id as TEST-200, and retains both rootA and rootB. The source registration still explicitly binds rootA to TEST-100. This silently attributes another ticket's usage to TEST-200 and persists it in subsequent snapshots.

Evidence: Disposable native CLI probe /tmp/al68-behavior-sol-01-probe.py, final fixture /tmp/al68-behavior-sol-01-bg_eer8l/project. Output: `TICKET_COPY {'ticket': 'TEST-200', 'owners': ['rootA', 'rootB']}`. Both sources carry actual fixture cwd; each registration was created and bound through native commands with an exact request token. The probe initially generated each ledger, copied A over B and republished B. No malformed source or guessed project attribution is required.

Refutation checked: validateGenerationProject checks source and ambiguous stores plus project, but accepts the registration without comparing r.TicketID to the active ticket. It does not receive that ticket. validateCaptureSelection rejects explicit source selection against a conflicting binding, but registered-only publication skips that selector path; retained baseline owners survive merge. Reconcile correctly selects B only and therefore does not repair the imported A baseline. Checking the ledger header alone would catch this particular copy; owner bindings must also remain enforced when a header already names the destination ticket.

Classification: The manual baseline ticket-override weakness exists in base de31cb1 (cached sessions were appended without this guard). This candidate introduces the automatic publication path and a new ownership validator that still fails the explicitly approved exact-ticket baseline contract. Thus this is an existing weakness exposed through the new path and an unmet required contract, not a claim that all behavior originated in this diff. High confidence, Linux native CLI reproduction; no real harness attribution claim.

Required correction: Validate the loaded ticket and every retained owner's verified ticket association against the requested ticket, preserving only properly accepted same-ticket baseline facts. Reject ambiguity without silently relabeling it.

### B2 — P1: Continuous callbacks can indefinitely postpone the periodic publication pass

Locations: backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture_worker.go:101-102; backend/internal/adapters/capture/worker.go:17-18; scheduling caller backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture.go:137-148.

Trigger: Supported lifecycle/context callbacks arrive more frequently than debounce_ms. Every successful receive/request/bind/reconcile updates the same project-wide requested_at. The periodic worker checks its due condition only together with age since the latest callback.

Expected: The periodic/coalesced worker publishes available source facts on a bounded cadence while a root is active. A busy callback stream may coalesce work but must not require global silence before any snapshot, including snapshots for another ticket in the same project.

Observed: With valid refresh_ms=100, debounce_ms=100, 82 supported UserPromptSubmit callbacks over 2.015 seconds prevented both canonical ledgers from being created. A ledger appeared promptly after callbacks stopped. All fixture source facts had already been available before the stream began. This spans about 20 refresh intervals. Default debounce_ms=500 has the same predicate if callbacks keep its global timestamp younger than 500ms at each worker poll; OpenCode session.updated/status/context events offer another reachable stream. Actual prolonged real-harness starvation was not measured.

Evidence: Same disposable native CLI probe and final fixture. Exact output: `CONTINUOUS_CALLBACKS {'seconds': 2.015454034990398, 'callbacks': 82, 'ledger_A_exists': False, 'ledger_B_exists': False}`; then `AFTER_QUIET {'ledger_A_exists': True, 'ledger_B_exists': False}`. The latter is sampled as soon as A appears, not a claim B fails after quiet. To start a foreground worker without racing a detached launcher, the probe seeded only the disposable publication_request table/generation with the production schema, then observed worker ownership through native status. All subsequent refresh postponement was caused by actual native receive commands; source/test checkout untouched.

Refutation checked: `due` already accounts for elapsed refresh time, but line102 still ANDs it with latest-request debounce, so the periodic branch cannot bypass starvation. Durable generation acknowledgement protects in-flight updates but does not bound time to start a pass. The lifetime branch cannot guarantee a successful pass either; a worker with no successful pass can stop pending at its deadline. Existing native crash/live-generation tests use debounce_ms=0 and cannot detect this failure.

Classification: Introduced native scheduler defect. High confidence in code and controlled CLI behavior; synthetic timing configuration, not evidence of an actual forty-minute runtime. Severity reflects loss of the core active-session publication guarantee until a quiet interval.

Required correction: Bound coalescing delay independently of last callback (for example an earliest outstanding deadline or a periodic refresh deadline that is not reset by later requests), retaining generation safety.

### B3 — P2: Automatic publication ignores disablement once a worker exists

Locations: backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture.go:134-145; backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture_worker.go:19-47,138-139,196-203; backend/cmd/agentic-lens/main.go:72-82.

Trigger: A native worker is active; user sets telemetry.capture.enabled=false in local YAML. Current worker retains its startup policy. Its generate subprocesses resolve current config but never reject capture-auto when disabled. At healthy lifetime handoff the new worker loads Enabled=false, yet command worker enters captureWorker unconditionally.

Expected: Disabling automatic publication must stop automatic writers within a bounded documented interval. It cannot depend on manually identifying/killing a process or waiting for all roots to become terminal.

Observed: After setting enabled=false, the same foreground native worker remained alive and advanced the canonical ledger updated_at from 2026-11-02T14:45:59.059777+00:00 to 2026-11-02T14:45:59.606561+00:00 during the following 0.7 seconds. These are local publication times, not source facts. The probe had stopped callback activity before disablement. It therefore demonstrates writes by the existing worker, not delayed newly launched callbacks.

Evidence: `DISABLED_WHILE_RUNNING {'before': '2026-11-02T14:45:59.059777+00:00', 'after': '2026-11-02T14:45:59.606561+00:00', 'advanced': True, 'worker_alive': True}` from the same final probe. Static handoff trace establishes that next worker activation also has no Enabled gate. Existing callbacks only use Enabled to suppress RequestPublication/LaunchWorker. The installer's disable/uninstall removal does not cancel existing workers either, so removing future activation entries alone cannot stop their periodic writes.

Classification: Introduced scheduler/configuration integration defect; high confidence. Dynamic cadence/summary changes also remain latched until handoff, but this finding is limited to disablement, for which even a fresh handoff does not enforce the resolved setting. No claim that arbitrary config hot reload is otherwise required.

Required correction: Enforce disabled policy at the automatic publication boundary and worker entry/continuation with a clear bounded stop behavior; preserve manual generate/recovery support.

### B4 — P2: Status errors for a valid registry without an automatic request table

Locations: backend/internal/adapters/capture/worker.go:28-34; backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture.go:168-170.

Trigger: enabled=false; receive/request/bind creates a valid registration registry without scheduling automatic publication. Run capture status. This also applies to an existing registry predating the new request table until a scheduling event creates it.

Expected: Status reports bindings, enablement and absence of pending automatic work; it must remain usable when automatic publication is disabled.

Observed: Native status exits nonzero: `Capture: SQL logic error: no such table: publication_request (1)`. Independently observed during the second disposable probe attempt before adding the request-table seed. The valid disabled registry and native request/bind sequence had all succeeded first.

Refutation checked: Open/OpenProject creates registrations/project_owner but not publication_request. Only RequestPublication creates this table, and the Enabled guard prevents that call in this case. PublicationRequest treats sql.ErrNoRows as empty but not a missing table. Status's no-state branch only handles absent registry.db, so it does not cover this valid state.

Classification: Introduced diagnostic compatibility regression. High confidence, native observed error plus exact creation/read trace. It obstructs the documented troubleshooting/binding inspection path while disabled. Fix should represent absent request state without requiring automatic activation; keep status read-only expectations.

## Other consequential hypotheses assessed

- Same physical directory contributors: canonical output lock is acquired before baseline/source reads; cumulative exact-owner replacement, durable generation ACK and shutdown unlock/recheck preserve the intended in-flight model. Metadata conflict resolver rejects differing explicit titles/types deterministically rather than accepting last-row order. Did not find an additional blocker in these paths.
- Independent directories sharing a store/ticket: ProjectState uses canonical directory namespaces; copied registry project_owner is rejected; source ValidateProject verifies cwd containment and nearer configured/Git project boundaries. Selector conflict checks use canonical store and per-owner source validation. These guard against the obvious cross-directory imports; B1 concerns different tickets within the same directory, not a false claim those directory guards fail.
- Source failure and cache reuse: unchanged fingerprint reuse still validates owner first; unavailable refresh marks failed/pending and leaves accepted snapshots. Baseline validation retains accepted same-project associations when source becomes unavailable. Freshness and checkpoint precedence are surfaced instead of silently overwriting newer canonical data. Scoped inspection did not establish another stale-cache defect.
- Publication: journal staging/recovery and lock-before-baseline path are shared by automatic/manual generation. Report-disabled branch retains prior report and replaces summary link with explicit stale-report text. No automatic deletion requirement was inferred from unapproved iteration03.
- Install/context: additive owned hooks/plugin retain unrelated configuration; project is captured into installed callback arguments and Codex binding guidance; OpenCode bind derives sessionID from runtime tool context. Trust remains human controlled. Static protocol checks do not prove actual callback delivery.

## Verification and evidence limits

Executed `cd backend && go build -o /tmp/al68-behavior-sol-01-native ./cmd/agentic-lens`: PASS. Executed the final standalone Python CLI probe: PASS as a probe runner (it reports incorrect product behavior above). It creates an isolated Git fixture and Codex JSONL source records, uses disabled capture for setup, manual/native automatic generation for ticket-copy proof, then native worker/receive for timing and disablement. Reproducer: /tmp/al68-behavior-sol-01-probe.py. Final fixture: /tmp/al68-behavior-sol-01-bg_eer8l. Probe workers/generators were stopped only after matching the exact owned binary and project arguments; final /proc inspection found no remaining worker using the probe binary.

## Findings

### B-01 — Automatic publication permits a bound ticket with no explicit title

- Severity: Major
- Location: `backend/internal/adapters/capture/store.go:215-231`; `backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture.go:254-268`; `backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture_worker.go:125-137`; `backend/cmd/agentic-lens/main.go:174-176`
- Trigger: bind a session with an explicit request token and ticket ID but omit `--ticket-title` (the CLI accepts this; the title is conditionally written only when nonempty). The automatic worker obtains an empty title from `CaptureTicketMetadata`, omits `--ticket-title`, then invokes `generate --capture-auto`.
- Violated expectation: contract requires explicit ticket/context and no guessed metadata. The prompt asks for a human-readable title, but the binding command does not enforce it. `--capture-auto` bypasses generate's existing missing-title rejection.
- Consequence: canonical ledger and summary can be automatically published with a valid ticket ID but missing ticket title. This silently weakens user-visible metadata and the explicit-context contract.
- Evidence: source trace above; `CaptureTicketMetadata` returns empty title without error when all bound registrations lack one. Generate's title guard is explicitly disabled under `capture-auto`.
- Disposition: introduced by the automatic path. Require a title at binding or make missing title an actionable pending state before publication. No product files modified.
- Confidence: high; static path is direct and unguarded.

### B-02 — Disabling/removing hooks does not stop an already-running publication worker

- Severity: Major
- Location: `backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture.go:97-114,139-150`; `backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture_worker.go:19-47,101-151`; `backend/internal/adapters/capture/install.go:174-183`
- Trigger: a lifecycle callback launches the native worker; while it is still within its configured lifetime, invoke `capture disable`/`uninstall` or change the local capture policy to disabled.
- Violated expectation: disabled state should prevent further automatic publication. Remove-mode install changes only owned harness files and records a disabled manifest; it does not revoke publication requests, communicate cancellation, or cause a running worker to reload/check current policy. The worker keeps its startup policy value and loops until idle/lifetime conditions, periodically invoking `generate` for registered tickets.
- Consequence: automatic ledger/summary updates can continue after the user disables capture or removes hooks. In particular, source growth during the remaining worker lifetime can be published despite the new disabled state.
- Evidence: `capture disable` reaches `Install(... Remove:true)` and returns without worker coordination. Worker starts from `captureWorker`, uses the passed policy for loop bounds and cadence, and does not re-resolve `ResolveCapture` or inspect manifests/disable state within the loop. This is a concrete source-level reachable path; not reproduced against an installed live harness.
- Disposition: introduced. A disable transition needs to invalidate/cancel worker ownership and make publication recheck enabled state before each pass/commit.
- Confidence: high for source behavior; runtime timing/disable race not separately exercised.

## Consequential hypotheses assessed

- Coalesced in-flight events: `RequestPublication` increments durable generation before launch; a second launcher that loses the kernel lock exits while the existing worker observes the newer generation and acknowledges only the captured generation after a successful pass. Idle shutdown releases and rereads generation before exit. No defect established in this path from source inspection.
- Same-directory multiple roots: reconciliation selects all bound ticket registrations, snapshots are per identity, and merge collision checks prevent conflating duplicate canonical IDs. Reviewed relevant path; no independent defect established.
- Independent directories sharing ticket/source store: project state namespace incorporates canonical project directory, source project metadata is verified during selection/reconciliation, and worker output is constrained to that project. No cross-import defect established in inspected flow.
- Partial source/publication failures: reconciliation retains prior snapshots on extraction errors; CLI publication journal/lock path recovers interrupted output. Existing evidence includes `/tmp/al68-iter02-test-report-02.md`, but this review did not rerun broad suites.
- Disabled summary/report behavior: existing code explicitly replaces report link copy when detailed report is disabled and does not automatically delete an earlier report. No defect established there.

- Reused CLI/race test evidence from `/tmp/al68-iter02-test-report-02.md` and the task-provided OpenCode/Codex runtime notes; did not repeat full suites or integrated `make`.
- Actual OpenCode probe observed one real 1.19.5 Linux path (root/native child/two directories with shared store and ticket, including SIGKILL restart), but not the actual 40-minute runtime. Real Codex 0.166 hooks require human trust; trust action is pending. SubagentStart on prior exec path and active/interrupted children before Stop were unobserved; Windows/Darwin cross-builds are not runtime evidence. These are acceptance gaps, not additional confirmed code findings.

The paths differ as strings, so seen[target] fails to detect their overlap.

Expectation/consequence: reject overlapping physical destinations before visible writes, including aliases of a not-yet-created leaf. The existing canonical-project/nearest-ancestor resolver demonstrates the needed distinction; do not rely solely on EvalSymlinks of the complete path. Preserve the prior accepted set on rejection.

Unprotected output overlap was already possible before this iteration; not claimed as a novel historical corruption behavior. It violates the current guarded publication consistency boundary. ## Findings

None.

## Hypotheses investigated

1. **Cross-project contamination through same ticket/store or caller-supplied project flags.** `ProjectDirectory` canonicalizes physical paths; `ProjectState` namespaces state by the canonical project; `OpenProject` binds the DB to that project. Registration refresh revalidates each owner against native Codex metadata or OpenCode session directory. `ValidateProject` rejects paths outside the project and nested `.git`/config boundaries. Generation locks and validates destinations before baseline reads, and cached owner sessions must be registered and revalidated. The callback's configured project cannot substitute for native source evidence. No concrete cross-project path found.

2. **A partial or failed source refresh erases accepted facts, or a fingerprint shortcut falsely marks an owner current.** In `refreshTicketOwners`, failed owner validation/extraction retains the prior snapshot and sets failed/pending status; results report per-owner coverage. A fingerprint shortcut requires successful owner validation, matching nonempty fingerprint, a nonempty accepted snapshot, and matching project association. Snapshot replacement additionally passes revision/time ordering. The numeric-token maximum is not used as a source-freshness rule. This supports accepted-fact retention with visible degradation.

3. **Publication can read a stale baseline before acquiring ownership, lose a callback arriving during a pass, or expose a silently mixed ledger/report/summary after interruption.** `runGenerate` takes the canonical per-output lock before recovery, baseline loading, source reconciliation, and publication. The worker acknowledges only the generation it observed before its pass; a later request remains unacknowledged. The journal records prior artifact presence/content and is retained until restoration or commit completes; native readers check the marker under the publication lock. These paths support the stated recoverable transaction model, without promising atomic visibility to arbitrary external readers.

4. **Completed time is derived from source invocation completion, or an active root blocks publication finalization.** Generation explicitly assigns top-level `completed_at` to the observability finalization time (`updated_at`) after source facts are reconciled. Per-invocation timestamps remain source-derived. Parent runtime evidence reports schema v5 and exact equality of these top-level timestamps; synthetic test evidence checks source growth and preserved invocation times.

5. **Automatic publication omits same-directory roots, repeatedly adds cumulative snapshots, overwrites conflicting ticket metadata, or mixes roots from distinct project directories.** Reconciliation iterates every bound owner for that project/ticket and replaces snapshots by exact owner identity after source ordering checks. Project state is isolated by canonical directory even when ticket and source store match. Title/type collection rejects multiple explicit values; worker leaves the publication pending when metadata conflicts. OpenCode source and ledger comparisons support same-directory roots/children and distinct-directory isolation.

6. **Child discovery or legacy state aliases can manufacture ownership or discard supported evidence.** Codex children are queued/recovered from source paths and validated against authoritative source metadata before inheriting a proven parent binding; OpenCode children use source parent evidence and source project directory. Canonical source-store aliases resolve to the same identity while distinct stores remain separate. Legacy unscoped state is preserved for explicit recovery and is not silently imported into project state. No source path derives identity from branch, title, time, role, Git common directory, or caller flag.

7. **Codex hook payloads misattribute native child IDs or an unavailable optional enrichment hides an accepted ledger.** `ReceiveCodex` treats `SubagentStart`'s session ID as the parent, queues opaque agent correlation separately, and queues a child path only at `SubagentStop`; no direct agent-id-to-session-id conversion occurs. Existing baseline facts remain available on optional source refresh failure, with source limitations visible. Scoped code verdict: **CHANGES_REQUESTED**.
Runtime/parent-integrated gate: **INCOMPLETE**, independently of the code defects below. This review does not authorize delivery or merge.

Run: iter02-architecture-sol-01; phase: discovery; focus: architecture. Requested profile: codex / gpt-6.1-sol / high. Requested settings are attribution supplied by the coordinator, not independently measured model identity. Usage and cost unavailable.

No sibling reports or shared review conclusions were read. No subagents. Only this report and isolated `/tmp/al68-architecture-sol-probes` evidence were written; product/test/configuration files remained unchanged.

## Blocking findings

### ARCH-01 — P2: Disabled capture does not stop a worker or its replacement chain

Locations: `backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture_worker.go:47`, `:196-201`; `backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture.go:134-144`.

Trigger: automatic publication already has a healthy active worker, then the user sets `telemetry.capture.enabled: false`. The callback launch defer checks Enabled, but the worker loop never does and holds its original policy. At lifetime it launches another worker unconditionally after a successful pass. The replacement loads the now-disabled policy and still enters the same publication loop. Thus an active registration can sustain publication and process replacement indefinitely after capture is disabled. This also survives the original process's finite lifetime; it is not merely an in-flight write completing.

Observable consequence: ledger/report/summary continue to be rewritten despite disabled automatic publication. The configuration flag controls only launches from callbacks, not the lifecycle owner that actually performs publication.

Evidence: disposable `TestReviewDisabledWorker` seeds an exact-source registered owner, durable request and idle activity, sets Enabled=false before launching the same native worker command used by replacement, and observes three successful ledger/summary publications before normal idle exit. This isolates the successor behavior without leaving a detached process chain. The ongoing-active handoff follows directly from the unconditional LaunchWorker at line 201. The probe does not claim to have run an indefinite chain.

Expected correction: enforce disabled policy at worker entry and before further publication/handoff, with a defined policy-change observation boundary. Preserve pending associations and accepted artifacts. Do not rely solely on suppressing future callback launches.

Classification: introduced implementation/required-policy defect. Confidence: high; native reproduction plus traced production handoff. The probe directly invokes the internal worker entry to represent a successor, rather than claiming the user must do so in normal operation.

### ARCH-02 — P2: Installed state paths drift silently from YAML/default command resolution

Locations: `backend/internal/adapters/config/capture.go:37-48`; `backend/internal/adapters/capture/install.go:231` (frozen `--state-dir`); `backend/internal/adapters/capture/plugin.ts:8-13`; `backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture.go:112-119` (absent-current-state status fast path).

Trigger: install using YAML state_dir=old-state, then change the same project's machine-local state_dir to new-state. Installed hooks/plugin retain the old absolute project namespace as a CLI override. ResolveCapture accepts it without comparing the installed association to current configuration. Manual generate/status/reconcile without that old override use the new namespace.

Observable consequence: collection and automatic publication stay on the old registry while ordinary commands see a different registry. Status reports generic absence of registrations rather than the incompatible installed path. Existing canonical owners can then fail baseline association checks in manual recovery. Merely reinstalling against the new namespace also cannot locate the old manifest to perform owned removal/upgrade; the old installation is not discovered through the new configuration.

Evidence: disposable `TestReviewInstalledPathDrift` performs actual OpenCode installation in an isolated project with publication disabled, changes local YAML, resolves the frozen callback override and default command policy, and runs real capture status. Both resolutions succeed with different paths; status exits successfully with `No lifecycle registrations. Install hooks...`, with no drift diagnosis. No real harness/plugin was started. Installer source confirms absolute freezing for both harnesses.

Requirement: approved iteration02 PLAN, Configuration/state/report policy: configuration changes or incompatible installed paths must be diagnosed and must not silently split collection and publication across registries. CLI override precedence is legitimate, but no distinction currently exists between an intentional new override and stale captured installation configuration. The documentation's instruction to review/reinstall paths does not implement that required diagnosis.

Expected correction: retain intentional override behavior while detecting installed-path/configuration disagreement and exposing actionable recovery through a stable installation discovery/ownership boundary. Do not silently migrate or discard old accepted facts.

Classification: introduced required-contract gap. Confidence: high; native installation/status probe and resolver trace.

### ARCH-03 — P2: Capture chooses process cwd while the existing project loader chooses the owning configuration directory

Locations: `backend/cmd/agentic-lens/main.go:62-85`; `backend/internal/adapters/config/capture.go:18-20`; unchanged `backend/internal/adapters/config/loader.go:436-470`; `backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture.go:424` (validateCaptureSelection project resolution).

Trigger: run manual generate from an ordinary `src/` subdirectory of a configured project, selecting a source whose authoritative cwd is the project root. The normal configuration loader traverses upward and loads the root project configuration, but the new capture resolver/project identity uses the process subdirectory. Source ownership validation then compares the root source against `src/`, rejecting it. State policy also silently falls back to subdirectory defaults because ResolveCapture reads only files directly under its supplied directory. Output at the normal root workspace would be rejected even earlier as escaping the wrongly selected project.

Observable consequence: an existing supported configuration-discovery invocation cannot generate the same project's ledger; CLI configuration and capture identity disagree about which project is selected. This is not the intended rejection of a distinct nested configured project.

Evidence: disposable `TestReviewGenerateFromSubdirectory` uses one exact-source fixture and identical absolute source/output arguments. Root-cwd control succeeds. With only cmd.Dir changed to its unconfigured `src/` child, generate exits 1 with `Capture ownership conflict: selected source owner root: source project directory conflicts with configured project`. Output is inside src in both cases, so this reproduction reaches actual source ownership rather than an output escape guard.

Expected correction: resolve the owning configuration directory once, canonicalize that physical project directory, and share it across capture policy, source validation, output validation and state selection. Preserve explicit rejection of genuinely separate nested projects. The same resolver should honor existing supported configuration filenames; Load currently supports yaml/yml/json while ResolveCapture reads only the yaml filename.

Classification: introduced compatibility/required shared-resolver defect. Confidence: high; root control and native failing invocation.

### ARCH-04 — P2: Status cannot inspect a valid registry before its first publication request

Locations: `backend/internal/adapters/capture/worker.go:28-34`; `backend/internal/adapters/capture/store.go:63`; `backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture.go:168-170`.

Trigger: an existing iteration01 registry, or successful receive/bind/reconcile while automatic publication is disabled, has registrations but has never called RequestPublication. Only RequestPublication creates publication_request. Store.Open does not initialize that table; PublicationRequest handles an absent row but not an absent table. New status calls it unconditionally.

Observable consequence: capture status exits 1 with `SQL logic error: no such table: publication_request (1)` instead of returning registrations, installation/trust and worker diagnostics. The required diagnostic/recovery command becomes unusable for valid pre-worker state and upgraded compatibility state.

Evidence: disposable `TestReviewStatusBeforePublication` creates a valid source-backed registration and binding using existing fixture helpers, then executes real capture status with the exact project/state. It reproduces the SQL error. No worker or callback is launched. The no-registry fast path does not refute this: registry.db exists in the affected case.

Expected correction: initialize operational schema at its owning store boundary or safely return no request for pre-request registries; preserve existing records. Add coverage for status before first request and upgraded state.

Classification: introduced schema-initialization/CLI compatibility defect. Confidence: high; native reproduction.

## Other consequential hypotheses assessed

- FCIS: new capture config validation, binding, metadata selection and checkpoint comparisons remain pure domain functions. Filesystem, SQL, clocks, process launch and locks stay in CLI/adapters. No blocking dependency-direction violation found in scoped changes. Moving orchestration from CLI solely for file size would be a maintainability suggestion, not a delivery blocker.
- Cross-process output ownership: main acquires canonical output ownership before baseline and source reads; alias normalization and kernel lock lifetime prevent stale pre-lock readers from publishing later. Native public ledger readers take the same lock. Generator uses the explicitly owned read API rather than reacquiring its own lock. No recursive lock defect found on these paths.
- Publication interruption: BeginPublication records a bounded prior set before visible writes; recovery rolls back before baseline reads, markers remain on failure, report digest binds to published ledger, and disabled detailed-report policy does not delete prior reports. This is recoverable publication, not atomic visibility for arbitrary external readers or physical power-loss proof.
- Events during a pass: generation is captured before work and only that generation acknowledged; later requests remain pending. Idle shutdown releases ownership then rereads pending state. Healthy lifetime handoff and failed-pass termination have distinct paths. Disabled-policy lifecycle remains ARCH-01.
- Scope and retained facts: ProjectState uses canonical physical-directory namespaces; OpenProject rejects copied ownership; source ownership and child proof are independently checked. Verified baseline associations let unavailable enrichment preserve accepted data, while unknown legacy owners fail visibly. No additional confirmed cross-project import was found in those inspected paths.
- Work bounds: source extraction has session/byte budgets and durable rotating class/owner cursors; native generation has subprocess timeout and remaining-lifetime bounds. Activity proof uses a separate byte allowance. Registry List decodes all stored snapshots repeatedly, and per-ticket work is performed sequentially; this review does not establish a constant memory/total-work bound independent of registry size. That remains a scaling observation, without a measured supported-load failure to elevate into a separate blocker.
- Explicit metadata: conflicts are detected independent of registration order; missing title remains unable to publish schema-v5 output. No permission to infer source identity or collapse independent roots was introduced by that resolver.

`cd backend && go test -overlay /tmp/al68-architecture-sol-probes/overlay.json ./cmd/agentic-lens -run '^TestReview' -count=1 -v`

### P2 — Configurable source work is not actually bounded

**Location:** `backend/internal/domain/capture_config.go:25-27` (`CaptureConfig.Validate`).

**Trigger:** A project sets `telemetry.capture.max_sessions` or `max_source_bytes` to any positive value above a practical limit, including the maximum representable integer. `Validate` rejects nonpositive values but has no upper bound for either field. `ResolveCapture` accepts this configuration, and the worker passes both values into `generate`/reconciliation as its per-pass work budget.

**Observable consequence:** A single native worker pass can be configured to inspect an effectively unbounded number of sessions or consume an effectively unbounded source-byte budget. This defeats the contract that the native scheduler has bounded work and exposes callback-triggered background processing to avoidable CPU/memory/IO exhaustion. The pass timeout is a separate wall-clock bound and does not cap the size of reads or allocations within that interval.

**Evidence:** The accepted configuration surface advertises these as `max_sessions` and `max_source_bytes`, requires bounded worker work, and sets finite defaults (256 and 64 MiB). The candidate's validator only checks `MaxSessions < 1` and `MaxSourceBytes < 1`; both fields are then used as reconciliation budgets. This is a direct source trace; I did not run a huge-budget stress probe.

**Classification/confidence:** Introduced contract defect, high confidence. Add documented finite ceilings (and validate duration-to-`time.Duration` conversions consistently) before accepting configured values. Exact ceilings are a product/configuration decision; they should be explicit and tested.

- **FCIS:** Reviewed changed domain config/value types and adapter/CLI worker paths. Capture policy validation is pure in `domain`; filesystem, clock, process and source operations remain in adapters/CLI. No domain I/O boundary violation found in the inspected paths.

Callback-launched workers detach from callback pipes/process groups. No concrete lost-generation or duplicate-owner defect found by source trace.
- **Publication/reader ownership:** Generation acquires the output lock before baseline/source reads; it stages a prior-good artifact journal and readers check the journal. The implementation explicitly documents recoverable rollback rather than portable atomic multi-file replacement. No conflicting lock order found in the inspected path.
- **Project identity/config compatibility:** Project-specific registry namespaces are keyed by canonical physical directory; registration source context is revalidated. CLI capture policy overlays defaults, shared YAML, local YAML, then explicit state override. Legacy unscoped state remains available for explicit recovery. No concrete cross-project mixing issue found in the inspected paths.

The only repository operation with execution effects was building the candidate CLI to a disposable /tmp binary. All dynamic fixtures and database mutations were isolated under /tmp.

## S-01 — High / P1: journal recovery accepts arbitrary out-of-project destinations

Location: backend/internal/adapters/publication_set.go:150-157 (RecoverPublication); caller backend/cmd/agentic-lens/main.go:108. Introduced by this candidate. Confidence: high, native CLI reproduction.

Trigger: a project-local `<ledger>.publication-pending` contains an absolute artifact path outside the configured physical project, with `present:true` and attacker-chosen base64 data (or `present:false` for removal). The operator subsequently runs ordinary generate against the in-project ledger. A copied crash journal with old absolute paths can also cross project boundaries without malicious alteration.

Observed consequence: recovery overwrites the outside file as the invoking user, even when generate subsequently fails because no project configuration exists. The marker is accepted without proving its project, ledger, original transaction or authorized member ownership. The attacker only needs to supply repository data, not executable code, a trusted hook, shell interpolation or filesystem write access to the external victim. This is a file-write/delete boundary violation, not a claim of OS privilege escalation.

Evidence: /tmp/al68-security-sol-8l2d5anj/results.json, journal section; reproducer /tmp/al68-security-sol-probes.py; binary /tmp/al68-security-sol-probe-bin built from frozen candidate. Project /tmp/al68-security-sol-8l2d5anj/project, ledger journal-ledger.json. Victim /tmp/al68-security-sol-8l2d5anj/outside-project.txt initially contained `accepted outside bytes`; after generate it contained `replaced via journal`. Command exited 1 with `Recovered interrupted publication: restored prior accepted artifact set before source reads`, followed by missing-project-configuration error. Only a disposable victim was touched.

Refutations checked: main.go validates the CLI ledger/summary destinations before recovery, but those checks never inspect the journal's artifact paths. Publication lock prevents concurrent publication, not malicious or relocated journal destinations. Recovery limits bytes/member count and requires absolute paths; none establishes destination authority. Mode 0600 for newly created journals does not authenticate a journal supplied as project data. Native direct process launch and human-controlled hook trust are irrelevant to this path. Existing happy-path crash tests exercise only self-produced valid journals.

Required correction: validate the complete recovered set against the current physical project and authorized artifact ownership before performing any member mutation; reject relocated/foreign/escaping members, including symlinked parents. Bind recovery metadata to the ledger/transaction rather than trusting absolute path strings. Retain diagnosable recovery state when rejecting it; do not discard accepted data as the repair strategy. Add an isolated rejection oracle showing outside files remain byte-identical.

## S-02 — Medium / P2: baseline validation omits exact ticket ownership

Location: backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture_worker.go:204-244 (validateGenerationProject), especially 234-242; caller main.go:237-247 and registered-only path main.go:269. Classification: inherited missing baseline ticket check, exposed by new automatic publication path and left unresolved by new ownership validator. Confidence: high, native CLI reproduction.

Trigger: a same-project ledger for TEST-1 is copied to TEST-2's destination, or a prior output path is accidentally reused. The registry correctly binds thread-01 to TEST-1 and thread-02 to TEST-2. Automatic generate for TEST-2 loads the copied baseline. Validation checks session/source uniqueness and physical project but never compares the ledger ticket or registration TicketID against the requested ticket.

Observed consequence: the output is relabeled TEST-2 and retains both thread-01 and thread-02. The explicit conflicting binding rejection in validateCaptureSelection is bypassed for cached owners: registered-only generation refreshes TEST-2 owners while preserving the foreign-ticket baseline owner. No registry forgery, unknown source context or cross-project session is needed. This is ticket data contamination and possible disclosure into a different ticket's published artifacts, not a prohibition on explicitly binding another session as an operator.

Evidence: /tmp/al68-security-sol-8l2d5anj/results.json first demonstrates copied baseline relabeling without a TEST-2 owner. Stronger /tmp/al68-security-sol-8l2d5anj/baseline-bound-result.json records valid independent TEST-1/thread-01 and TEST-2/thread-02 ownership, copied a.json -> poisoned-b.json, and successful `generate --capture-auto --ticket-id TEST-2 --ticket-title 'Different owner' --ticket-type chore --json-output <project>/poisoned-b.json`. Exit 0, ledger ticket TEST-2, sessions [thread-01, thread-02]. Automatic worker subprocesses use this generate shape. No detached worker was run. The stronger probe initially hit a legitimate ambiguous-store guard because S-03 had deliberately added a duplicate registration; removing only that isolated probe registration restored the normal two-ticket precondition and reproduced the defect. This refutation and fixture correction are preserved in the result.

Required correction: validate requested ticket against the loaded ledger's explicit ticket and each known baseline owner's binding before reuse. Fail visibly without changing baseline bytes when ownership conflicts. Preserve accepted same-ticket facts with unavailable enrichment; missing current source must not erase already verified ownership. Cover copied same-project/different-ticket baselines in addition to existing cross-project-copy rejection.

## S-03 — Medium / P2: supplied Codex transcript bypasses source-store proof

Location: backend/internal/adapters/capture/project.go:117-135 (ValidateOwner); producer hooks.go ReceiveCodex -> Store.Register; consumer reconcile.go extractExact. Classification: pre-existing transcript/store association gap, still present in newly added exact ownership enforcement; required-contract defect. Confidence: high, native receive/bind/reconcile reproduction.

Trigger: installed receive is configured with Codex home B while its authoritative callback transcript actually comes from Codex home A (misconfiguration, home transition, or mismatched payload). The supplied path names a valid same-project/same-ID transcript. ValidateOwner consults Store only when TranscriptPath is empty; with a supplied path it checks ID/cwd but never establishes the path belongs to that store.

Observed consequence: receive and exact-token binding succeed and reconciliation marks that session `current` under the empty, unrelated home B. The same actual session can therefore obtain a separate identity/request/ticket scope through another purported store; wrong-store ownership is asserted as verified instead of rejected/unresolved. Explicit operator ticket binding is permitted; it should not manufacture a different source store for the transcript.

Evidence: /tmp/al68-security-sol-8l2d5anj/store-result.json and /tmp/al68-security-sol-store-probe.py. `--store /tmp/al68-security-sol-8l2d5anj/wrong-empty-codex-home`, payload transcript `/tmp/al68-security-sol-8l2d5anj/source/sessions/fixture.jsonl`, ID thread-01, same physical project. Receive exit 0; exact returned token bind to TEST-3 exit 0; reconcile exit 0 reports source codex/store wrong-empty-codex-home/session thread-01 with state current and revision 2738. Original thread-01 was already bound TEST-1 under actual home A. Only synthetic local records were used. Initial probe tried capture status in a capture-disabled fixture and encountered missing publication-request state; changed the investigation to a read-only SQLite query for the issued request token rather than repeating the failing hypothesis or modifying product code.

Refutations checked: canonicalIdentity normalizes the claimed store but does not bind the transcript file to it. ID/cwd guards correctly reject foreign projects and IDs; they do not refute same-ID/same-project/wrong-store acceptance. Manual exact discovery is scoped to store and does not have this bypass, whereas callback and queued child paths can provide direct paths. Alias handling should continue to accept true physical aliases; arbitrary paths and different homes must not be conflated.

Required correction: establish exact physical store membership/provenance for supplied transcript paths, including queued child paths, before marking ownership/source facts current. Use store-backed lookup or equivalent supported provenance validation that rejects different stores and escaping symlinks while preserving legitimate archive paths and true aliases. This finding asserts data integrity, not local-code privilege escalation.

## Other consequential hypotheses assessed

- Project/source cwd: ProjectState hashes the canonical directory; OpenProject pins owner directory; ValidateProject resolves aliases, rejects outside paths and nearer .git/config project markers. Independently validated children go through inheritChild -> validateOwner. Manual family selection validates each emitted owner, not just the parent. Existing tests target sibling/nested directory and child rejection and copied-project baseline. No additional bypass demonstrated beyond S-03's store binding.
- Per-session requests: cryptographically random per-identity token; Bind requires exact request; conflicting tickets fail. OpenCode binding uses runtime context.sessionID and argument arrays; it does not accept a model-supplied source/session override. Codex shell prompt values are quoted and IDs constrained. Operator cross-session binding is explicitly permitted by the contract; status/request access is not an authentication boundary against arbitrary same-user code. No unsupported privilege escalation finding.
- Process/installation: worker uses exec.Command with argument arrays and selected executable, plugin uses execFile, install JSON-encodes template values once and quotes static Codex commands. Installed paths target native executable; wrapper downloads/updates remain explicit distribution work rather than callback behavior. No network, shell wrapper, recursive model or trust approval added to native worker path. Passing an explicitly chosen binary to installation executes it by design; no escalation claim. Install preserves unknown hook groups, checks exact owned groups/plugin hashes before upgrades/removal, and records conflicts rather than silently removing edited content. Did not probe arbitrary code supplied by an already authorized same-user binary.
- Path checks: ticket binding restricts traversal characters; CLI output guards canonicalize symlink ancestors. The journal bypass is distinct from ordinary CLI destination guards. No concurrent symlink attacker race was claimed without a separate supported boundary.
- Privacy: hook JSON is size-bounded and stores only selected fields; registration JSON omits raw snapshots/transcript paths from published report, report redacts token/store/project, errors for source refresh are generic, and snapshot persistence uses PersistAnomalySummaries. Journals necessarily contain prior artifact bytes as base64 plaintext (not encryption); current durable staging creates mode-0600 files. No claim that base64 is secret protection, no raw transcript probe, and no separately substantiated new transcript leak. Journal provenance/destination is S-01. Existing accepted files can contain user prose; retention of that prose is not itself an invented privacy defect.
- Legacy/copied state: project-owner mismatch is rejected; legacy unscoped state is retained with diagnostics; unavailable verified same-project associations remain readable. No demand for destructive reset or universal fresh-source rereads. S-02 concerns known conflicting ticket ownership, not absent enrichment.

## Verification and limits

Executed: candidate CLI build `go build -o /tmp/al68-security-sol-probe-bin ./cmd/agentic-lens` from backend, exit 0; isolated native journal, baseline and callback/store probes above; start/end exact-byte comparison of all 48 frozen files, zero differences. No full suite rerun without a concern that required it.

Reused supplied verification: full CLI race test PASS 26.394s (/tmp/al68-cli-final-10.txt; bounded unchanged source recorded in tester handoff), tighter lifecycle twice (/tmp/al68-cli-lifecycle-11.txt), adapter/domain/config/source race evidence (/tmp/al68-corrections-tests.txt), vet, 14 distribution probes, native CLI checks, and integrated make /tmp/al68-iter02-integrated-make-01.log (frontend 35 files/781 tests, production build and native cross-build tail inspected). These are positive regression evidence, not coverage of the three negative cases above. TestMain native CLI build is ordinary build, not race-instrumented; race evidence for adapter/tests is separate.

Read supplied source-comparison JSON /tmp/al68-iter02-codex-source-02.json: interactive plus exec independent roots and one source-proven native child, exact source project/tokens/model/parent matches, own root bindings, no agent generate, schema5/report digest. Accepted the brief's updated OpenCode comparison/restart evidence rather than treating the older author report's Codex limitations as current truth. No live global stores queried. These runtime observations do not prove all callback events or non-Linux support. SubagentStart observation, active/interrupted child before Stop, real forty-minute runtime and physical power-loss guarantees remain unverified as stated in the brief. No iteration03 behavior is required. Parent must consolidate and decide remaining acceptance after addressing these code findings.

# Security review: iter02-security-luna-01

- Phase: discovery; requested profile: codex / gpt-6-luna / medium. Requested settings are recorded; observed runtime model identity/settings were not independently available.
- Candidate: candidate-02-01, frozen against de31cb1; archived diff SHA-256 `17e8ee67d3140080d30f11cb7f430a6d82925191cb400aaf87c537ec66ba7de7`.
- Scope: security boundaries in the 48 frozen paths, especially project/source/session ownership, output/recovery paths, request binding, local state and installation trust.
- Integrity: all 48 current source paths matched the frozen copies at review start and end. No source/test/runtime/config writes were made.

## Finding

### SEC-01 — High — Recovery journal can overwrite arbitrary absolute paths

**Location:** `backend/internal/adapters/publication_set.go:128-163` (`RecoverPublication`); ordinary recovery is called by `backend/cmd/agentic-lens/main.go:108` before source reads.

**Trigger:** A user invokes `generate` with an in-project `--json-output` while a `.publication-pending` journal exists beside that output. The journal is JSON controlled by whoever can write project files and carries `priorArtifact.Path` as an absolute path. Recovery checks only that the path is absolute; it does not bind journal members to the requested ledger, report, or summary destinations, nor constrain them to the project. It then calls `durableReplace` on each recorded path.

**Consequence:** A malicious or untrusted project can plant the journal and make a later normal generation overwrite any file writable by the invoking user, including shell startup/configuration files. A first-generation absent member can also cause recovery to remove an arbitrary path. This is a distinct project-data-to-user-file boundary; it does not assume arbitrary code execution already exists.

**Evidence:** Disposable probe under `/tmp/al68-journal-probe-Zu4I46`: created an in-project `ledger.json.publication-pending` with a single absolute destination pointing to a disposable sibling `outside/victim.txt`, then ran the shipped `bin/agentic-lens generate --ticket-id TEST-1 --json-output <project>/ledger.json --allow-empty`. The CLI reported recovery and the sibling file changed from `victim-original` to `attacker-restored`; generation then exited because the probe config lacked required source roots. The recovery write occurred before that unrelated validation error. No shared project file was modified.

**Classification/confidence:** Introduced in this candidate's publication journal implementation; high confidence, directly observed on the candidate binary. A filesystem principal already able to write the invoking user's files is outside the threat model; an untrusted project contributor able to place project data is a realistic boundary here. Fix requires validating journal ownership and every destination against the canonical expected publication set (and safe path identity) before any restoration/removal; reject invalid journals without performing writes.

## Disposition of other assigned hypotheses

- Project identity: `ProjectDirectory`, `ProjectState`, `OpenProject`, and `ValidateProject` canonicalize paths and bind state to the physical configured directory; source checks use Codex rollout metadata or OpenCode session context. Reconciliation revalidates registered owners before refresh. Did not establish a separate ownership bypass.
- Binding: bind requires the current per-registration request token; source and session are explicit arguments, and project state is scoped. I did not treat an operator explicitly selecting a session/ticket as a privilege escalation. No separate cross-project path from selection to published facts was demonstrated.
- Destination paths: the generation caller validates ledger and append destinations against the configured project, including symlink resolution. This does not protect recovery journal members, which are the finding above.
- Install/process behavior: native invocations use argument arrays; Codex shell commands quote arguments and reject control characters, OpenCode plugin arguments remain arrays. Installation edits harness configuration additively and records owned entries for removal; it does not grant harness trust. No separate executable/argument injection or trust bypass was substantiated.
- Raw payload/privacy: hook input is size bounded, and callback feedback avoids echoing untrusted raw payloads. Persisted session snapshots contain telemetry facts; no distinct confidentiality defect was confirmed in this focused pass.

## Reused evidence and limits

Reused the supplied CLI/component/full `make` evidence; no broad suite was rerun. The targeted CLI probe used disposable paths and the candidate's existing binary. It demonstrates recovery behavior, not a physical crash. Non-Linux native runtime, Codex SubagentStart observation, and active/interrupted-child-before-stop remain unverified per the supplied brief; these are runtime acceptance gaps, separate from this code defect.

## Verdict

**CHANGES_REQUESTED** for the scoped security code review due to SEC-01. This verdict is independent of parent/runtime acceptance; no delivery or merge approval is implied.

# iter02-release-sol-01

Run: iter02-release-sol-01. Phase: discovery. Candidate: candidate-02-01 against de31cb1, exact archived diff /tmp/al68-iter02-candidate-01.diff and 48 source copies under /tmp/al68-iter02-candidate-01-xf13oa7x. Requested settings: codex / gpt-6.1-sol / high. Runtime metadata supplied to this reviewer identifies the Codex harness, gpt-6.1-sol, high; no independently measured usage or cost is asserted.

Scoped code verdict: CHANGES_REQUESTED. Three verified findings below: one introduced worker shutdown defect and two existing installer defects conflicting with current accepted requirements. Overall runtime/parent-integrated gate: INCOMPLETE and owned by parent; this report does not grant delivery or merge approval. Existing make PASS is reused verification, not final review approval.

The 48 frozen source files were compared byte-for-byte against their archived copies before investigation and after all probes: 48 matched at both boundaries, zero mismatches. No persistent source hashes were added. Initial Git status contained staged product changes, parent ticket edits, staged unapproved iteration03, and untracked consolidated review artifacts. These were preserved and the latter conclusions were not read. Iteration03 was excluded from requirements; the existing detailed capture report is retained by default and its removal is not requested.

## Findings

### RELEASE-01 — P1 / high: disable/uninstall leave the native publisher active

Location: backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture.go:97-114 and backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture_worker.go:47-63, 196-201. Related: backend/internal/adapters/capture/install.go:174.

Trigger: a bound active session already has a running automatic worker when the user successfully runs capture disable or capture uninstall for its source. The native removal branch updates owned activation files and writes Active=false, then returns. It neither revokes automatic publication nor coordinates shutdown with the worker. The worker never reads manifest activation or rechecks an enablement signal. It continues refreshing every cadence; healthy active work can launch a replacement worker at its lifetime boundary. policy.Enabled only gates launches from receive/request/bind/reconcile; worker entry itself ignores it.

Expectation: owned disable/removal reverses the installed automatic collection/publication activation while retaining accepted data for recovery. A successful disable must not leave an automatically self-renewing publisher modifying ticket artifacts without new integration events.

Consequence: disabling a live integration still reads source data and rewrites ledger/report/summary. State retention plus active registration keeps it alive after the producer callbacks have been removed, so future Stop/idle events may never arrive to terminate its activity. The finite lifetime is not a shutdown guarantee because the healthy worker hands off.

Proof: /tmp/al68-release-sol-probe.py, successful disposable project /tmp/al68-release-sol-qx0gbx3r. Native executable /tmp/al68-native-corrections matched the author-recorded final executable SHA256 93665757590ee5f97bb999b2a32d09beec1ce3d23836cbf22fd4d0a0ef8d4444. Probe installed owned Codex hooks in a project with spaces, made an explicit request/bind, seeded only disposable registry scheduling/transcript-path fields corresponding to the existing native worker test fixture, and started a separate process-group native worker. It produced input=10; capture disable returned 0 and the manifest became inactive. Only afterward synthetic source usage was updated to input=30 with a later source timestamp. The worker remained alive and published input=30, including repeated subsequent passes. This is an actual Linux native process/publication observation using synthetic source, not another real Codex runtime claim. The probe killed and reaped its isolated process group in finally; no shared candidate worker was launched.

Refutation sought: removal does preserve unrelated hooks and accepted local state, and dry-run correctly does not disable anything. Those guards do not communicate deactivation to the existing worker. A pass already in flight could reasonably finish, but repeated periodic passes and lifetime handoff have no deactivation check at all. The code also routes uninstall through the identical Remove=true branch; the native probe directly exercised disable, with uninstall impact established by that common branch.

Classification: introduced in iteration02 native scheduling; new discovery in this run, not an original iteration01-only defect. High confidence. Needs durable deactivation/shutdown semantics that preserve manual recovery and other-source ownership, with a native live-worker removal regression. No unsolicited service/watchdog is required.

### RELEASE-02 — P2 / medium: true project aliases cannot reinstall or remove the same installation

Location: backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture.go:71-90,110; backend/internal/adapters/capture/install.go:135-149.

Trigger: install with --repo /physical/project, then reinstall/disable/uninstall with --repo /alias where alias is a symlink to that same directory (or reverse). CLI resolves state namespace from canonical ProjectDirectory but passes the original repo spelling to Install. Install uses filepath.Abs rather than canonicalization and compares manifest.Repository with that string.

Expectation: approved true-alias normalization and idempotent additive reinstall/removal, without collapsing distinct physical directories.

Consequence: the second command finds the same canonical manifest then refuses it as another repository. A user cannot upgrade or remove activation through an equivalent supported project spelling; this is an operational recovery failure, not data contamination.

Proof: same successful probe, initial native install returned 0; reinstall with the symlink path returned 1, 'Capture: capture manifest belongs to another repository'. Both paths resolve to the same directory; state path is the identical projects/location namespace. Paths contained spaces. No harness trust was changed.

Refutation sought: ProjectState correctly canonicalizes aliases and manual selection has an alias regression. Neither protects Install because the canonical project variable is not passed to its Repository option. This is not a sibling/nested-project refusal and should not weaken those guards.

Classification: original/pre-existing absolute-path manifest comparison exists at de31cb1; iteration02's canonical state routing exposes it through the default path as well. New discovery here; existing required-contract defect, not claimed as a newly authored comparison. High confidence. Canonicalize installation ownership consistently and add alias reinstall/removal coverage.

### RELEASE-03 — P2 / medium: native install resolves default source configuration from caller cwd instead of --repo

Location: backend/cmd/agentic-lens/capture.go:104-110,281-295; relevant unchanged dependency backend/internal/adapters/config/loader.go:436-468,516-570.

Trigger: native capture install --repo /configured/project --source codex (or opencode), omitting --store so the supported configuration resolver applies, from outside that project. captureSourceStore calls config.Load("") and therefore searches caller cwd, whereas capture policy and state use the selected project.

Expectation: configured project source locations resolve for the selected installation project; an explicit source/store wins, but omission must not silently borrow a different project's source configuration/default.

Consequence: successful install permanently embeds a different source-store path into all callbacks. Exact ownership guards may subsequently reject/miss the real sessions, leaving capture pending or failed despite successful configuration. A caller's unrelated invalid configuration can also prevent setup/removal of the requested project.

Proof: disposable project local YAML explicitly configured telemetry.sources.codex.home to /tmp/al68-release-sol-qx0gbx3r/source. Running native install --dry-run --source codex --repo that project, without --store, from the disposable parent returned 0 but generated all hook commands with --store /home/niltonduarte/.codex. The configured local source was not used. Only dry-run output was inspected; the real source store was never opened or modified by this probe. The --store explicit control used in initial install generated the intended path.

Refutation sought: the shipped downloaders require explicit --capture-store and therefore avoid this defect; documentation recommends explicit source paths. Native command help nevertheless makes --store optional for install and the implementation explicitly invokes source configuration fallback. ResolveCapture(project,...) is correct for state/cadence but does not change captureSourceStore's cwd. Both harness branches share the wrong config load; Codex was directly probed.

Classification: original/pre-existing at de31cb1, new discovery in this run; required configuration/installation contract gap, not introduced by iteration02. High confidence. Resolve omitted source settings from the selected canonical project, or explicitly reject omission rather than accepting the caller's unrelated project configuration.

## Independent path investigation and checks

Read the assigned reviewer persona, shared context, canonical review procedure, technical guidelines, regression checklist, AL-68 CONTRACT and approved iteration02 PLAN. First-pass hypotheses were formed from source before consulting /tmp/al68-iter02-corrections-02.md. No sibling report or iter02 REVIEW/FINDINGS/REVIEW_RUNS conclusion was consulted.

Inspected both shipped downloaders, both wrappers, embedded native installer/plugin, CLI capture argument/config routing, project/state canonicalization and ownership validators, worker launch/process separation, worker loop/shutdown/transfer, source fallback and relevant tests; followed manual/setup/operator instructions and unchanged Makefile/release workflow entry points. This is a release/setup-focused candidate review, not whole-repository correctness certification.

- Native binary boundary: install validates capture protocol using a bounded process; Codex commands quote each argument and OpenCode uses execFile with argument arrays and explicit project/state. Worker processes invoke the current native executable and pass explicit project/state, with generation child cwd set to the project. The OpenCode imports use the existing harness runtime, not a separately installed Node service. Native Go embeds the plugin and web distribution; release targets build the native executable after frontend preparation. No Go/Node build toolchain is needed in an adopting repository.
- Wrapper capture dispatch exits before missing-binary downloading or update checks. Wrapper-self-as-native recursion is rejected. Capture-aware host updates compare successful protocol output before replacement; foreign installed platforms are preserved with an actionable diagnostic. The downloader stages candidates/backup wrapper and binaries and rolls back on later setup failure; native installer separately rolls back owned configuration. Existing original source files and unrelated harness hooks are preserved by ownership checks. These findings do not require a new installer framework.
- Compared shipped copies: wrappers are byte-identical. Downloader differences are naming, skill-root resolution and default destination; capture install/upgrade transaction logic is shared text. The direct manual native install and PowerShell upgrade guidance explicitly retain/probe/restore the previous handler; protocol success alone is not advertised as runtime proof.
- Source ownership and destination checks were traced through ProjectState, ValidateProject, ValidateOwner and ValidateDestination. State namespaces use canonical physical project directories, not Git common directories. Traversal/symlink output escape rejection and nearer-project guards were not relaxed. Detailed report remains enabled by default; explicit suppression retains prior files and removes fresh summary linkage. No request for report removal is made.
- Unix launch uses a separate session and disconnected file streams; Windows has detached creation flags. Kernel worker locks, durable per-project generations and observed-generation ACK protect normal overlap; shutdown rechecks pending generation after unlock. Crash recovery is event-driven rather than an always-running supervisor. This trace explains the removal defect rather than treating smoke/config as proof of all lifetimes.
- Native probe setup initially failed because a disabled callback had not created publication_request, then because request alone lacked a transcript path. Those failed probe attempts establish no product assertion. After inspecting their worker logs, the final isolated fixture explicitly seeded those scheduling/path fields, matching existing test fixture responsibilities. All worker process groups were cleaned up even on those failures. This probe does not purport to test a fresh real harness interaction.

Reused verification rather than rerunning broad suites: /tmp/al68-corrections-distribution.txt (14 passes, both shipped shell entrypoints; transport/handler fixtures, not public release download proof); /tmp/al68-corrections-native-cli.txt (native worker tests pass); /tmp/al68-cli-final-10.txt and /tmp/al68-cli-lifecycle-11.txt per frozen brief; /tmp/al68-corrections-tests.txt and vet evidence; /tmp/al68-iter02-integrated-make-01.log (full integrated gate including frontend/native builds). Also reused documented Darwin/Windows cross-build results. No new full make or release publication was run. Release workflow source and local build evidence do not establish execution of a new GitHub release or a verified download from that future release.

New execution: native capture install help; disposable installation/dry-run/alias/native worker probe above; byte comparisons at start/end. No product/test/config/runtime changes in shared checkout, staging, commits, pushes, telemetry, subagents, trust edits, global writes or external release actions.

## Runtime/support limits and parent handoff

Actual Linux evidence is distinct from fixture and build evidence. /tmp/al68-compare-final-result.txt reports source-verified OpenCode 1.19.5 owner/project/native-parent/token/cost/digest/schema/timestamp comparisons, project0 10 owners including four native children and project1 two independent roots sharing ticket/store; workers eventually stopped. The brief's supported-event SIGKILL restart and actual Linux evidence is reused, not re-enacted.

Read /tmp/al68-iter02-codex-source-02.json: Codex 0.166 Linux, normally user-trusted hooks, interactive/vscode-classified root plus exec root and one native child; exact source identity/project/model/usage/parent comparisons and own root binding, no agent generate, ledger/report match, schema5 and snapshot completed_at. It explicitly excludes cross-directory Codex/non-Linux and active/interrupted-child-before-Stop/universal SubagentStart claims. The observed source lacks effort/cost in some records; these remain unknown. Existing operator support table is conservative and does not broaden these observations into universal capture.

SubagentStart and active/interrupted-child-before-Stop remain UNVERIFIED. Non-Linux evidence is build-only: native process lifetime, Windows executable replacement, detached callback behavior and filesystem crash semantics still need actual host evidence before broader claims. Minutes-long real runtime and synthetic forty-minute source timestamp growth are different evidence. Native worker SIGKILL is not physical power-loss proof, and journal interruption tests are not filesystem atomicity guarantees. No mandatory Git/CI service, worktree feature, release publication, harness trust bypass or draft iteration03 policy was introduced as a requirement.

Parent should resolve RELEASE-01 and reconcile the two verified existing installer contract defects, then request affected revision-aware checks. Preserve the real runtime limitations independently of code corrections; existing make/runtime successes do not waive these findings or establish overall final approval.

# Release/setup review report

- Run: `iter02-release-luna-01`
- Phase: discovery
- Candidate: `candidate-02-01`, frozen against `de31cb1` (diff `/tmp/al68-iter02-candidate-01.diff`, SHA-256 `17e8ee67d3140080d30f11cb7f430a6d82925191cb400aaf87c537ec66ba7de7`)

- Scoped verdict: **CHANGES_REQUESTED**
